title: RFID Coin Tag — Small HF/UHF Asset & Loyalty Disc
summary: RFID coin tags pack an HF (ISO 14443 / ISO 15693) or UHF (ISO 18000-63 / GS1 EPC Gen2v2) chip into a 10-30 mm disc, 2-4 mm thick, with epoxy or ABS encapsulation rated IP67/IP68. They suit tool-crib and FOD programmes, calibrated-instrument tracking, gym / locker / laundry loops, loyalty and cashless-payment tokens, amusement / leisure tap-points, and product-authentication anchors — the cases where space on the host item is the binding constraint and a pocket-size disc is the cleanest mechanical fit.

brief.label: Form factor
items: Disc 10-30 mm diameter × 2-4 mm thick — pocket-scale token, 0.8-3.5 g typical mass.
Optional 3-5 mm ferrite spacer lamination for on-metal UHF performance without changing the disc footprint.

brief.label: Air interface envelope
items: HF 13.56 MHz — ISO 14443 Type A/B (MIFARE Classic 1K, MIFARE DESFire EV3, NTAG 424 DNA) or ISO 15693 (I-CODE SLIX2).
UHF 860-960 MHz — ISO 18000-63 / GS1 EPC Gen2v2 ({chip:impinj-m730:name} / M750, {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name}).

brief.label: Housing and durability
items: Epoxy-encapsulated disc or injection-moulded ABS / PC disc with ultrasonic weld seam.
IP67 (HF authentication) or IP68 (laundry, aquatic leisure) ingress rating, -25 °C to +85 °C service.

brief.label: Attach methods
items: 3M VHB adhesive (3M 4910F / 5952) to non-porous host surfaces.
M3 / M4 through-hole screw mount via central bore (tool handles, gauges).

brief.label: Read range
items: HF contactless tap — 0-40 mm against phone / reader head.
UHF in free space 0.5-2 m; with ferrite spacer on steel tool body 0.3-1.5 m.

brief.label: Crypto options (HF)
items: NTAG 424 DNA SUN message with CMAC — 1-tap authentication of consumer product / loyalty token.
MIFARE DESFire EV3 AES mutual auth for staff tokens and regulated cashless wallets.

brief.label: Tool-crib / FOD use case
items: Tool-return handshake at portal ≤ 100 ms per tool; batch read 20-40 tools on a tray.
Ties into aerospace FOD programmes where 100% tool accountability is required before closing a panel.

brief.label: Loyalty / cashless use case
items: Gym / spa / pool / locker token; amusement-park pay-per-ride cashless wallet; laundry-room wash-cycle credit.
Tap-time budget ≤ 300 ms including reader auth + POS round trip.

brief.label: Regulatory / conformance envelope
items: FCC Part 15.225 (HF) and Part 15.247 / 15.249 (UHF); RED 2014/53/EU; ISED RSS-210 / RSS-247.
Payment-adjacent tokens respect PCI PTS domain separation — the coin does not carry cardholder data, it addresses a tokenised wallet at the POS.

brief.label: Materials compliance
items: ABS / PC housing halogen-free; REACH SVHC screen; RoHS 3 (2015/863) compliance on chip + antenna foil + housing.
Food-contact-incidental grade epoxy available for hospitality and kitchen-tool variants (FDA 21 CFR 175.300).

brief.label: Integration / encoding
items: Factory TID is read-only per ISO 18000-63; EPC / NDEF payload locked with lock / permalock command after WMS encode.
EPCIS 2.0 commissioning event writes GIAI / GRAI / SGTIN or token-ID into ERP on first read.

brief.label: Mounting matrix
items: Five mount paths: M3 / M4 screw via central bore, blind rivet, 3M VHB adhesive, weld-on 316L carrier plate, recess embed with structural adhesive pot.
Metal host → on-metal UHF spacer variant fixed by screw / rivet / weld; non-metal host → any mount. Adhesive is the no-drill path, recess embed the flush path.

heroPoints: Disc 10-30 mm × 2-4 mm — fits on hand tools, calibrated instruments, loyalty tokens and small product housings where larger tag geometries do not fit.
ISO 14443 + ISO 15693 + ISO 18000-63 / GS1 Gen2v2 covered in the same form factor — one SKU family answers tool-crib FOD, cashless leisure and product-authentication in one catalogue.
IP68 epoxy or ABS disc survives tool-crib abuse, 80 °C commercial dish-wash and pool-chemistry exposure without antenna delamination.

sections.title: Why pocket-scale assets are the hardest items to keep track of
bullets: Hand tools, gauges, jigs and calibration instruments are the most frequently lost and borrowed-without-return items in any industrial operation — 10-15% annual tool-loss rates are routinely reported in manufacturing and MRO under manual logging.

Barcode labels on hand tools are destroyed within days by grease, abrasion and solvent exposure, and manual barcode check-out imposes 30-60 s per transaction — so workers bypass the system and 40-60 % of tool movements go unrecorded.
Calibration-controlled instruments must stay inside their calibration date and chain of custody; losing either creates quality escapes and audit findings under ISO 9001 7.1.5 / ISO 17025.

Aerospace FOD programmes require 100 % tool accountability before closing an aircraft panel, while leisure and loyalty operators fight the same fight in chlorine: paper tickets and magstripe cards fail exactly where a sealed coin token keeps reading.

items.label: UHF read range free space; 0.3-1.5 m on-metal with spacer
Tool-return handshake per tag at portal

sections.intro: Nobody audits a pocket. That is the whole problem: hand tools, gauges and tokens are small enough to walk, valuable enough to matter, and numerous enough that manual logging quietly gives up. If the estate is a tool crib, start with the [RFID tool-tracking solution](/solutions/rfid-tool-tracking/) — then come back for the disc that makes it stick.

sections.title: HF vs UHF coin tag — picking the right air interface
bullets: Dual-interface coins carry both an HF and a UHF antenna on the same 30 mm disc, at the cost of a slightly thicker 4 mm profile and a roughly 20-30 % free-space UHF read-range reduction.
sections.intro: Same disc, two radios, and no wrong answer — only wrong pairings: HF taps, UHF sweeps. The full portal-physics argument lives in the [HF vs UHF asset-tracking comparison](/compare/hf-vs-uhf-rfid-for-asset-tracking/); the coin-sized version is below.

before: The read is a deliberate tap — smartphone or reader head at 0-40 mm.
Authentication is the point: NTAG 424 DNA runs AES-128 SUN messages with a per-tap CMAC tied to the factory UID, on Common Criteria EAL4-certified silicon (per NXP).
The workflow is cashless leisure, loyalty or staff ID — mature POS integration and a simple phone tap path.
The host is metal but the read is close anyway — HF tolerates a metal boundary better at tap range than an unshielded UHF disc.
after: Reads must be hands-free — 0.5-2 m in free space, a full tool tray in one portal sweep.
The programme is tool-crib, FOD or MRO rack accountability at volume.
On-metal mounting is planned — the ferrite-spacer variant holds 0.3-1.5 m on a steel tool body.
Payload governance runs through lock / permalock EPC writes in a WMS / EPCIS pipeline.

sections.title: One disc, five mounts — matching fastener to host surface
sections.intro: The coin's pitch is that it goes on anything — but 'anything' spans a lacquered gauge handle, a chlorinated locker door, a bare steel weldment and a wooden crate, and each wants a different fastener. Pick by host surface and service life; the disc doesn't care which you choose, but your re-tagging budget does. (Casting into fresh concrete is its own discipline — that's the [concrete-embed tag](/products/rfid-tags/rfid-concrete-embed-tag/).)

rows: M3 / M4 screw (central bore)
Tool handles, gauges, jigs, racking — anything that can be drilled and tapped
Stainless cap screw + thread-locker
Strongest serviceable mount; shrugs off vibration and solvents; removable for re-issue when the host retires
Blind rivet (central bore)
Sheet metal, bins, totes and crates with one-side access
Stainless blind rivet sized to the bore
Permanent and tamper-resistant; faster than screws on high-volume lines; drill out to remove
3M VHB adhesive (4910F / 5952)
Non-porous, flat, clean surfaces — coated metal, glass, ABS / PC housings
VHB pad or two-part structural epoxy
No drilling and no torque spec; degrease before bonding; low-surface-energy plastics (PP / PE) bond poorly — prefer a recess embed there
Weld-on carrier (316L stainless variant)
Bare structural steel where drilling is prohibited — frames, fixtures, weldments
Tack-welded 316L carrier plate; disc retained by screw or epoxy
Keeps weld heat away from the chip; specify the stainless disc variant and clear the weld procedure with site QA
Recess embed
Wood, plastic and composite bodies — handles, pallets, crates, fixtures
Drilled recess + structural adhesive pot
Disc sits flush with the surface, nothing to snag on gloves or conveyors; permanent by design

image.alt: Mounting matrix for RFID coin tags: five side-view cross-sections show a coin disc fixed by M3 or M4 screw through the central bore, blind rivet, 3M VHB adhesive pad, tack-welded 316L stainless carrier plate, and flush recess embed with adhesive pot. A decision strip underneath states that metal hosts take the on-metal UHF spacer variant via screw, rivet or weld, while non-metal hosts accept any of the five mounts.

callout.label: Metal or not — the one-line decision
callout.text: Non-metal host: any mount, standard disc. Metal host: screw, rivet or weld the on-metal UHF variant (integrated ferrite spacer, 0.3-1.5 m on steel) — or go HF if the workflow is a tap anyway. Adhesive on coated metal is fine; bare steel that cannot be drilled is what the weld-on carrier is for.

sections.title: Diameter series — what each millimetre buys
sections.intro: Diameter is antenna budget: more millimetres buy more aperture and more range, and cost you fitment on the smallest hosts. The series below shares its resin and ratings with the wider [epoxy tag family](/products/rfid-tags/rfid-epoxy-tag/); for permanently steel-bound estates, read it alongside the [anti-metal tag](/products/rfid-tags/rfid-anti-metal-tag/) line.

sections.title: Where RFID coin tags earn their place in the catalogue

dataHighlight.heading: FOD and tool-crib capture once the coin sits on every hand tool
dataHighlight.text: Industry tool-crib data consistently reports 10-15 % annual tool-loss rates under manual logging. With an IP68 RFID coin glued or screwed onto each hand tool and a UHF portal at the crib door, the capture rate for check-out / check-in events rises above 99 % and annual tool-loss drops to low single-digit percent, because the handshake happens automatically and there is no incentive to bypass the system.
dataHighlight.source: Aerospace and MRO tool-control programme case studies summarised in Boeing and Airbus FOD-prevention guidance and in SAE AIR5562 Foreign Object Damage / Debris (FOD) Prevention Program, 2022.

sections.title: How to roll out an RFID coin programme without breaking calibration, payment or privacy

items.label: Week 1 — profile choice
items.text: Run a matrix of candidate host items (tool, instrument, token, product) against read-range and authentication needs; lock air interface (HF / UHF / dual) and chip choice (MIFARE DESFire EV3 / NTAG 424 DNA / I-CODE SLIX2 / {chip:impinj-m750:name}) per SKU.

items.label: Weeks 2-3 — encoding workflow
items.text: Stand up POS / WMS encode bench that writes a locked EPC / NDEF, issues a factory lock / permalock, and commits an EPCIS commissioning event to ERP. Validate the 100 % lock rate on the first 5,000 coins before scale-up.

items.label: Weeks 4-6 — portal + POS deployment
items.text: Deploy UHF portal at the tool-crib door (tool-FOD) or HF readers at leisure POS. Tune antenna power so portal reads the full tray with < 0.5 % miss rate and no read-leak through the wall to the adjacent zone.

items.label: Weeks 7-10 — compliance wrap
items.text: Tie the coin ID to ISO 9001 7.1.5 / ISO 17025 calibration records for the tool case, or to the PCI-scoped wallet for the cashless-leisure case. File DPIA / Art. 13 notice for the consumer-authentication case. Bring in internal audit for the first quarterly close.

items.label: Month 4+ — scale and reuse
items.text: Operating context extends to tool-crib, FOD, cashless-leisure and product-authentication programmes — review periodicity, refresh windows and audit obligations vary by vertical and are documented per estate. scale from pilot cell to 100,000 – 5,000,000 coins across multi-site operations, with EPCIS event stream → ERP → CMMS / POS / brand-protection analytics tying each coin to an asset, wallet or product identity.

sections.intro: Ten weeks from mounting matrix to steady state, if the boring parts happen in order. Below: the boring parts, in order.
checklist: Lock the air interface first: UHF on-metal coin for tool-crib / FOD, NTAG 424 DNA for consumer authentication, MIFARE DESFire EV3 for staff / cashless wallets, I-CODE SLIX2 for library / document loops.
Permalock the EPC / NDEF payload straight after WMS / POS encode — an unlocked coin is the single biggest failure mode in a brand-protection or cashless pilot.
Keep PCI PTS domain separation: the coin addresses a tokenised wallet at the POS and carries no cardholder data; the authorisation path stays inside the PCI-scoped reader.
Register tool-crib coins against ISO 9001 7.1.5 / ISO 17025 calibration records so the EPCIS event stream is the single source of truth for next-due date and last-used job.

For consumer-facing loyalty or authentication, publish a privacy notice covering the tap-event payload (ID + timestamp + venue) under GDPR Art. 13 or the regional equivalent — data minimisation is easy because the coin carries no PII.
Plan for loss: a lost coin costs USD 1-3 in the batch; the host tool, instrument or wallet value is what the coin exists to protect.

faq.question: Is the RFID coin tag waterproof enough for pool and laundry use?
faq.answer: Yes — the epoxy-encapsulated variant is rated IP68 per IEC 60529 and tolerates -25 °C to +85 °C plus typical chlorinated pool chemistry and 80 °C commercial dish-wash or laundry cycles. For continuous chemical exposure beyond that envelope, a 316L stainless or PTFE-overmoulded variant is available.

faq.question: Can a coin tag carry cashless-payment credit?
faq.answer: Not directly. The coin carries a token-ID that addresses a wallet at the POS; the wallet holds the balance inside a PCI PTS-scoped system. This domain separation keeps the coin outside PCI DSS scope while still delivering a 300 ms tap-to-pay leisure experience.

faq.question: How do I pick between HF and UHF for a loyalty / authentication programme?
faq.answer: HF (ISO 14443 / ISO 15693) is the natural choice when the customer taps a phone or POS head at 0-40 mm range and you want NTAG 424 DNA-grade authentication with a per-tap CMAC. UHF (ISO 18000-63 / GS1 Gen2v2) is the natural choice when you need handsfree portal reads at 0.5-2 m — FOD, tool-crib, MRO rack accountability. Dual-interface coins exist and cost a modest read-range penalty.

faq.question: What is the MOQ and lead time for RFID coin tags?
faq.answer: RFID coin tags run at MOQ 500-1,000 units for standard disc SKUs and 2,000-5,000 units for custom-shape, logo-embedded or colour-matched builds. Standard lead time is 3-4 weeks with a commodity NFC / UHF chip; a 2-week pilot build of 100-500 units is available to validate mounting and encoding before scale-up.

faq.question: Which mounting method should I use on a metal surface?
faq.answer: On metal, specify the on-metal UHF variant with integrated ferrite spacer (0.3-1.5 m read on a steel tool body) and fix it by M3 / M4 screw, blind rivet or the weld-on 316L carrier. Adhesive works on coated metal within the housing's service envelope; bare structural steel that cannot be drilled is the weld-on carrier's case. HF coins tolerate a metal boundary better at tap range and suit tap-only workflows.

faq.question: Can RFID coin tags be removed and reused on another asset?
faq.answer: Screw-mounted coin tags are designed for removal and re-issue: back out the screw when the host retires and re-register the coin's ID against the new asset in the EPCIS / asset system — the locked EPC travels with the coin, not the host. Rivet, weld-on and recess-embed mounts are permanent by design, and adhesive removal usually sacrifices the tape pad rather than the tag.

faq.question: Do RFID coin tags ship pre-encoded, or do we encode on site?
faq.answer: Both paths are supported. Factory encoding writes the EPC / NDEF payload, applies lock / permalock per ISO 18000-63 / GS1 Gen2v2, and delivers an EPCIS commissioning file keyed to the read-only factory TID. On-site encoding suits programmes that assign IDs at issuance — either way, lock the payload immediately after writing.

faq.question: Can the coin tag carry a logo or serial number?
faq.answer: Yes — laser-engraved sequential numbering and pad-printed logos are available on the epoxy and ABS disc faces, and engraving survives the same abrasion and chemical exposure as the housing. Colour-matched housings and logo-embedded builds fall under the custom MOQ tier of 2,000-5,000 units.
